transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith, welcome in. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m not sure if I’m saying this the right way, but… I came in because I just can’t seem to settle. It feels like I’m restless inside my own skin, like I need to get up and do the next thing even when I’m tired and I know I should be sitting still. It’s gotten hard to ignore.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications, especially antipsychotics or anti-nausea drugs, in the weeks before this restlessness began?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t started anything new that I can remember, and I don’t believe any doses were changed right before this. I’m sorry if that’s not very helpful—I can double-check if you need me to.
When you feel this restlessness, is it mainly a physical need to move your legs or body, or is it also accompanied by a lot of worried, anxious thoughts running through your mind?

It feels more physical, I think… like I just can’t settle in my own skin. I’ll be worn out and know I should sit still, but there’s this push to get up and do the next thing. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right.
When you actually get up and move or pace, does that give you any relief from the restless feeling, or does it stay just as intense no matter what you do?

It helps a little in the moment, I guess, but not really enough. Like I get up because I feel like I have to do the next thing, even if I’m worn out, but that feeling of not being able to settle inside myself is still there. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Has this restless, need-to-move feeling been something you've experienced since childhood, or is this a new feeling that started more recently?

I think it’s been there a long time, honestly… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but even in grade school my teachers would write things like I was bright, but careless. They’d say I lost papers, talked out of turn, and needed reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work. So… I guess it’s not completely new, if that helps?
Have you ever taken antipsychotic medications or anti-nausea drugs like metoclopramide or prochlorperazine at any time in your life, even years ago?

I don’t think so… I mean, not that I remember. Those names don’t sound familiar to me. I’ve had medicines here and there over the years, but I don’t want to tell you the wrong thing. Is that the kind of thing that would usually stand out on a medication list?

Do you notice these restless feelings and trouble focusing showing up in multiple areas of your life right now—like at work, at home, and in social situations—or is it mostly limited to certain settings?

It’s… it’s not just one place, no. I wish it were. I’m not working now, so I can’t speak to that exactly, but at home my family has had to help with bills and paperwork more than I’d like to admit.

And socially, too — at church and with the garden group, I’ve dropped the ball on things, and then other people have had to redo plans or cover what I said I’d do. I feel really embarrassed saying that, because I do care, and I don’t want people thinking I’m irresponsible. But I can tell they don’t feel they can count on me the same way anymore.
Do you find that you have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations, or that your mind easily wanders and you get distracted, even when you're trying hard to pay attention?

Yes… I do. I mean, I try, I really do, and sometimes I start out okay. But I can sit down with the senior center newsletter or the choir schedule, and after a few minutes I realize my eyes have gone over the same lines more than once and I don’t actually know what I just read.

It’s embarrassing to admit, because it sounds like I’m not trying, but I am. My mind just sort of slips off somewhere, even when I’m meaning to pay attention.

Have you ever had a distinct period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual, that was different from how you normally feel?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m more wound up or irritable than I’d like, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had several days of feeling euphoric or unusually full of energy like a totally different person.

Does that answer what you mean?
